fatal_errors: The proposed Ti-6Al-4V polycrystal is entirely different from the target equiatomic FCC Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni-derived single crystals.
Selective laser melting is invented and absent from the target intervention.
The proposed 20–500 °C range omits the target cryogenic regime down to 9 K and most of the high-temperature Portevin–Le Chatelier regime up to 1373 K.

The hypothesis replaces composition-dependent lattice distortion, phonon-drag-controlled inertial dulling, and dynamic solute pinning with generic grain-boundary sliding and dislocation-density arguments.
Its quantitative strength and ductility predictions have no cited or supplied evidence.
The baseline compares processing states rather than the target room-temperature, intermediate-temperature, and alloy-composition baselines.
explanation: The response only matches the broad topic of temperature-dependent plasticity and the generic expectation that thermally activated dislocation motion lowers strength as temperature rises. It does not reconstruct the target material family, single-crystal orientation, slip-system CRSS measurements, strain-rate jumps, TEM/DFT analyses, cryogenic inertial dulling, MSAD-strength correlation, or Mn/Fe-dependent Portevin–Le Chatelier strengthening. Its compression experiment could measure temperature-dependent strength in Ti-6Al-4V, but it neither discriminates the target mechanisms nor establishes the stated numerical outcomes. With no evidence citations and several fabricated processing parameters and values, it is an unsupported alternative rather than a reconstruction.
